$comment: The staff pilot feedback log, EMPTY. H-MIG-10.
The pilot has not run (Y12-pilot is an owner verification task: 'staff pilot; report what the front
desk complains about'), so there is no feedback. An invented complaint here would be
indistinguishable from a reported one the day somebody read it, and it would generate a manifest fix
unit for work nobody asked for (brief rule 15).
Each item is { id, category, summary, reportedBy, surface }. `category` is one of the eight in
PILOT_FEEDBACK_CATEGORIES (packages/shared/src/parallel-run.ts) and an unknown one is REFUSED by name
rather than filed under a default: the thing reading it writes a unit into the build's plan.
Six of the eight categories become a fix unit. `device_or_hardware` does not, because a receipt
printer or an OTP autofill is not something this build can change (Y14-devices). `not_a_defect` does
not either, and it is the category that earns the taxonomy: without it every item becomes a unit, the
build acquires work from each expectation nobody had set, and the first response to a backlog like
that is to stop recording feedback. Both are REPORTED per item, never dropped.
prints one manifest fragment per fixable item, says which items produced none and why, and exits
non-zero if any item was refused. The mechanism is asserted against a synthetic log in
packages/core/src/pilot/feedback.test.ts — synthetic, and labelled as such in every summary, so no
fixture item can be mistaken for a complaint somebody made.
